why_in_two_sentences: PsychCentral covers the standard arc (definition, why people invalidate, example statements, consequences, how to validate) with LMFT medical review, and the UR Rochester piece is a short LCSW blog on the same ground. Ours covers all of that plus the part that makes it a pattern: the half second spent computing which answer is reasonable, how the dismissing voice gets internalized, and what to do in the moment somebody dismisses you, with 34 verbatim FAQs.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Describes the internalized mechanism: you overrule your own reaction before anybody else gets a vote
The half-second scene (locating the reasonable answer instead of the feeling) is the most precise description of this pattern on page one
Explains why the dismissing voice ends up inside your own head and why it builds through small repetitions
Gives an in-the-moment response for when somebody dismisses your reaction, not just recovery advice
34 verbatim FAQs including the gaslighting differential, disagreeing-versus-invalidating, and the my-husband-dismisses-my-feelings case

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the repeated-dismissal-to-self-distrust mechanism, then four verbatim recognition moments; the reader is located before any scrolling.
above_the_fold.theirs: PsychCentral opens with validation defined first, then invalidation as its opposite, under a medical-review byline; clean and credible, but definitional rather than experiential.

trust_signals: PsychCentral shows medical review by an LMFT; UR Rochester shows a named LCSW author on a university-medicine domain; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: none - ours matches both competitors' definitional ground and exceeds it on mechanism, differentials, and verbatim long-tail coverage.
